Around 26.58% customers churned, while 73.42% customers stayed, showing a moderate churn level that needs attention.
Most customers are in the high monthly charges range (80–120), indicating the company mainly serves premium customers.
Very few customers are in the low monthly charges range (20–40).
High density in Total Charges (0–1000) suggests many customers are new or have low tenure.
Early-stage customers are more likely to churn.
Month-to-month contract customers show the highest churn rate.
One-year and two-year contract customers have better retention.
Low commitment contracts increase churn risk.
Customers using electronic check payment methods show higher churn compared to card or bank transfer users.
Electronic check users may have lower trust or weaker engagement with the company.
Customers without tech support are more likely to churn.
Customers without online security services show higher churn.
Customers without device protection also have higher churn rates.
Low service usage leads to lower customer engagement.
Paperless billing users show slightly higher churn compared to non-paperless billing users.
Paperless billing customers may be more flexible but less loyal.
Customers with low engagement and fewer services are more likely to churn.
Higher customer engagement improves customer retention.
